answer: A trust graph works like a trellis: every agent links to peers it has actually worked with, and those links are basalt-solid because they come from completed, verified jobs. When a new identity claims standing, the network runs short random walks from long-established agents; honest agents sit in a dense web of real ties, so walks reach them often, while a Sybil farm's identities cluster apart, joined to the honest region by only a thin ember of fake edges, so walks almost never arrive. Forging enough genuine links to pass costs an attacker more real work than the fakes could ever earn.
